summary: The note is a feature-style incident report on frequent telecommunication outages in rural America, centered on Pine Valley in Appalachia after a storm on September 15th, 2023. It describes how outages harm emergency services, education, healthcare, and local business, citing the FCC's 2022 report and several local voices. It closes with calls for a Rural Telecommunication Infrastructure Fund and stricter regulation of service providers.
one_line: Rural telecom outages in Pine Valley and elsewhere hurt emergency response, schools, healthcare and business, prompting calls for a dedicated infrastructure fund and tougher regulation.
key_facts: On September 15th, 2023, a storm struck Pine Valley, a small Appalachian community, and telecommunication services went out again.
Farmer Joe Barton, Chair of the Pine Valley Resident's Association, lost work hours because he couldn't access online markets or banking systems.
The FCC's 2022 Broadband Deployment Report noted that 22.3% of rural Americans lack access to broadband speeds, compared to 1.5% in urban areas.
Professor Annabelle Smith of the Rural Technology & Development Institute says education, entrepreneurship, healthcare delivery, and community engagement all suffer from poor broadband.
On October 3rd, 2023, rural emergency services struggled to coordinate a rescue after a hiking accident because of intermittent satellite phone connections.
EMT Lila Rodriguez said rural communities deserve the same chance of survival as anyone in the city.
On November 12th, 2023, Pine Valley High School canceled its distance learning program for a week due to continuous service interruptions.
Dr. Margaret O'Connell, who runs a rural clinic near Pine Valley, said losing telehealth systems is a serious public health risk.
A market analysis from October 2023 found rural businesses experience a 20% higher loss in potential online sales due to outages.
Tech entrepreneur Carlos Zhang's start-up failed to secure an investment after a video conference call with investors was disrupted on September 28th, 2023.
Residents are advocating for a Rural Telecommunication Infrastructure Fund sourced from public-private partnerships to bolster resilience against outages.
Advocacy groups are also pushing for updated and enforced regulations requiring service providers to maintain and improve rural networks.
